text:
camille: Heads-up — apiserver p95 spiked to ~3.2s in eu-west1 around 10:13 UTC, controller-manager restarted 3x. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ctlplane... :eyes:
leo: Yep seeing it. Correlates with a bunch of GPU attach events and a burst of watch requeues. apiserver logs show a lot of `500` proxy errors to provisioner.
sre-oncall: Oncall looking now, paging logs. Any network churn metrics?
infra-kevin: SNAT pool usage jumped in eu-west1 at the same time, a bunch of ephemeral ports exhausted on NAT gateway. Could explain proxy failures to provisioner endpoints.
camille: Interesting — controller-manager restart reason is `lease update timeout` in logs, followed by many list/watch errors. Paste of recent lines:
```
I0316 10:13:05.123 controller-runtime/manager] controller-runtime metrics server is starting
E0316 10:13:12.456 controller-manager] error syncing controller: apiserver error: 500 proxied: dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: i/o timeout
W0316 10:13:12.457 reflector] pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go/.../watch.go: Unexpected EOF
```
leo: Also seeing KV store latency climb in etcd leader metrics (proposal durations up). Might be that many attach operations are overwhelming backends?
maria: From provisioner side: attach RPC latency spiked when we saw dozens of attach requests per second for new GPU nodes in eu-west1 burst. Many were retries. Logs show `AttachVolume` latencies ~2-3s then timeouts.
sre-oncall: So chain: SNAT exhaustion -> proxy errors -> apiserver timeouts -> controller-manager lease drift -> controller restarts. Agree? :thinking_face:
infra-kevin: Looks right. NAT metrics: ephemeral ports used = 65520/65535 at 10:12:58. There was a short increase in outbound flow due to a large batch job that spun up many GPU pods in a short window.
camille: Can we mitigate quickly? Options: increase NAT port range, throttle attach retries at provisioner, or emergency failover of controller-manager to another region?
leo: Short-term I can patch provisioner to backoff more aggressively (reduce immediate retries) and drop attach parallelism per nodepool. Will push a canary ASAP.
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: rollout start provisioner/attach-backoff v1.3.1-canary @eu-west1
sre-oncall: Also request infra to temporarily expand NAT ports and add an extra NAT gateway to reduce collisions.
infra-kevin: Spinning up extra NAT gateway now and increasing ephemeral port range on eu-west1 NAT. ETA ~8 minutes.
maria: I'm adding stricter retries and jitter to attach RPCs in the canary. Will monitor error rate and attach latency.
camille: Thanks. Also open an incident ticket and mark as P2 — we had some customer-facing latency but no data loss. Link it here when created.
sre-oncall: Incident created: INC-2026-1483 https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1483 — summary attached.
leo: After the canary deploy, I'm seeing apiserver p95 drop to ~750ms and controller-manager stabilized. Watch requeues dropping. :thumbsup:
infra-kevin: NAT gateway provision finished, ephemeral ports now 131070 (double). No more port exhaustion spikes in last 2m.
camille: Great. Postmortem action items: 1) rate-limit attach bursts from autoscaler/provisioner, 2) autoscaler to spread attach start times, 3) monitor SNAT usage with alert at 80% for eu-west1, 4) consider regional NAT capacity runbook. Assign owners?
sre-oncall: I'll own alert and runbook update. infra-kevin owns NAT capacity. leo + maria will own attach backoff changes.
camille: Perfect. Closing thread once follow-ups are in GH issues. Thanks all. :heart:
